Building GhostTrace AI: An AI Investigation & Observability Platform That Explains Why AI Systems Fail Using OpenTelemetry and SigNoz

How I built an AI Investigation & Observability platform that traces every AI decision, correlates latency with business impact, and automatically generates investigation reports using FastAPI, OpenTelemetry, Gemini and SigNoz.

Dashboard view of GhostTrace AIThe Moment I Realized Traditional Monitoring Wasn’t Enough…
This is story-driven and naturally leads into why you built GhostTrace AI.
I wasn’t trying to build another monitoring dashboard.
I wanted to answer a much harder question:
When an AI application produces an unexpected response, how do you know what actually happened?
Traditional monitoring tools can tell you that a request failed or took too long, but they rarely explain why. They don’t reveal which AI agent slowed down, how many tokens were consumed, where latency increased, or how the final response was generated.
While building AI applications during the Agents of SigNoz Hackathon, I realized that AI systems need more than logs and metrics — they need investigations. That realization led me to build GhostTrace AI, an AI-native observability platform that automatically traces every reasoning step, identifies root causes, and generates investigation reports powered by OpenTelemetry, SigNoz, and Gemini.
Introduction
“Observability isn’t about collecting more data — it’s about understanding the story behind every request. SigNoz gave me the visibility to turn AI executions into explainable investigations.”
Artificial Intelligence is rapidly transforming the way modern software is built. From intelligent customer support and autonomous agents to AI copilots and recommendation systems, Large Language Models (LLMs) have become a core part of today’s applications. While these systems deliver impressive capabilities, they also introduce a new level of complexity. Unlike traditional software, AI applications make probabilistic decisions, rely on multiple services, consume tokens, invoke external tools, and often follow multi-step reasoning before producing a final response.
I participated in the Agents of SigNoz Hackathon because I wanted to explore a challenge that many AI developers face but is rarely addressed: understanding what actually happens inside an AI application when something goes wrong. During my previous AI projects, I could see whether an API request succeeded or failed, but I had very little visibility into the AI’s internal workflow. Questions such as Which agent caused the delay? Why did the response take longer than expected? How many tokens were consumed? Which reasoning step failed? were difficult to answer using traditional monitoring tools.
This experience made me realize that AI applications require a different approach to observability. Conventional monitoring solutions primarily focus on infrastructure metrics, logs, and HTTP requests. However, modern AI systems need much deeper insights into reasoning workflows, agent execution, latency, token usage, model interactions, and decision-making processes. Without this visibility, debugging and optimizing AI applications becomes increasingly difficult as they grow in complexity.
To address this problem, I built GhostTrace AI, an AI-powered investigation and observability platform that combines FastAPI, OpenTelemetry, SigNoz, and Gemini to automatically trace every stage of an AI workflow. Instead of simply displaying logs, GhostTrace AI reconstructs the complete execution path, analyzes each investigation, identifies potential root causes, measures AI performance, and generates actionable recommendations through an interactive investigation dashboard.
In this article, I will walk through the complete journey of building GhostTrace AI — from designing the system architecture and implementing a multi-agent investigation pipeline to instrumenting distributed traces with OpenTelemetry and visualizing them in SigNoz. Along the way, I’ll share the challenges I encountered, the technical decisions I made, and the practical lessons I learned while building an AI-native observability platform during the hackathon.

The Problem: Why Monitoring AI Systems Is Hard?
When we think about monitoring software, we usually imagine tracking CPU usage, memory consumption, API latency, or server uptime. Traditional observability tools excel at answering questions like:

• Is the service healthy?

• Which API is slow?

• Did the database fail?
For conventional applications, those answers are often enough.
But AI systems operate in an entirely different world.
Traditional Monitoring Stops at the API Boundary
Imagine a customer asks an AI assistant:
“Why did my payment fail yesterday?”

• The application successfully returns a response.

• The API responds with HTTP 200 OK.

• The server logs show no errors.

• CPU usage is normal.

• Memory usage is stable.
From the infrastructure perspective…
Everything looks perfect.
Yet the user receives a completely incorrect answer.
This is the fundamental challenge with AI applications.
The failure is rarely caused by infrastructure.
Instead, it happens inside the reasoning process of the AI agent — a place traditional monitoring tools simply cannot observe.
AI Applications Behave Differently from Traditional Software
Unlike deterministic software, AI systems are built as chains of intelligent decisions.
A single request may involve:

• Understanding the user’s intent

• Retrieving knowledge from memory

• Calling external APIs

• Querying vector databases

• Invoking multiple tools

• Generating reasoning with a Large Language Model

• Validating the final response
Each step contributes to the final answer.
Each step introduces new opportunities for failure.
Unlike traditional APIs, there isn’t just one execution path.
Every request can follow a completely different reasoning journey.
That makes debugging exponentially harder.
Logs Alone Cannot Explain AI Decisions
The first instinct when something goes wrong is usually:
“Let’s check the logs.”
Logs are useful.
But they answer only what happened, not why it happened.
Planner executed successfully
Knowledge Search completed
Gemini responded in 2.4 seconds
HTTP 200 OKEverything appears healthy.
But those logs cannot explain questions such as:

• Which reasoning step consumed the most time?

• Why were 4,000 tokens generated instead of 800?

• Which external service slowed down the response?

• Why did confidence suddenly drop to 72%?

• Why did one investigation cost four times more than another?
Logs
AI debugging requires understanding the entire execution journey.
The Missing Visibility Every AI Engineer Faces
While building my project during the hackathon, I realized that every AI request contains far more information than ordinary applications.
For every investigation I wanted to know:

• Which tools were executed?

• How long did each agent take?

• Which span introduced the highest latency?

• How many tokens were consumed?

• What was the estimated inference cost?

• What confidence score did the AI produce?

• Which reasoning step caused the issue?

• What should the engineer investigate first?
None of this information is available from infrastructure monitoring alone.
Without deep observability, debugging AI becomes guesswork.
Real-World Debugging Becomes a Detective Story
During development, I intentionally simulated different investigation scenarios.
Some requests completed successfully.
Others experienced:

• Slow tool execution

• High token consumption

• Reduced confidence

• Increased latency

• Elevated operational cost
At first glance, every API looked healthy.
Only after visualizing distributed traces inside SigNoz could I pinpoint the exact bottleneck.
Instead of reading hundreds of log lines, I could literally watch the AI’s decision-making process unfold — from Planner to Memory Search, Knowledge Retrieval, Gemini inference, Validator, and finally the Executive Report.
The trace transformed debugging from trial-and-error into a clear investigation.
That realization inspired the project’s name:
“GhostTrace AI — because every AI decision leaves behind an invisible trail. My goal was to make that trail visible, explainable, and actionable.”
The Question That Changed My Project
While debugging my AI workflow, I stopped asking:
“Did my API succeed?”
and started asking:
“Can I explain every decision my AI made?”
That single shift in perspective became the foundation of GhostTrace AI.
Instead of building another monitoring dashboard, I built an AI Investigation Platform that combines OpenTelemetry, SigNoz, and multi-agent reasoning to transform distributed traces into human-readable incident reports — helping engineers understand not just what happened, but why it happened.

Turning AI Telemetry into Actionable Investigations
Modern AI applications generate thousands of events, traces, logs, and metrics every day. While observability platforms collect this data efficiently, identifying the actual reason behind failures still requires engineers to manually inspect multiple dashboards.
I wanted to eliminate that manual investigation process.
GhostTrace AI is an AI-powered observability platform that automatically analyzes distributed traces, correlates telemetry, identifies root causes, estimates business impact, and generates actionable recommendations — all from a single investigation dashboard.
Instead of asking:
“Where do I start debugging?”
GhostTrace AI answers:
“Here’s what failed, why it failed, how severe it is, and how to fix it.”
Project Objectives

• Automate AI incident investigation

• Reduce Mean Time To Resolution (MTTR)

• Transform raw telemetry into business insights

• Visualize complete AI execution flow

• Generate AI-powered investigation reports
What is GhostTrace AI?
GhostTrace AI is an intelligent investigation assistant built on top of FastAPI, OpenTelemetry, and SigNoz. It continuously collects telemetry, analyzes distributed traces, and produces AI-generated investigation reports with confidence scores, severity classification, root cause analysis, and recommended actions.
Target Users

• AI Engineers

• DevOps Engineers

• SRE Teams

• Platform Engineers

• Engineering Managers
Core Features

• 🔍 AI-powered Root Cause Analysis

• 📊 Real-time SigNoz Observability Dashboard

• 🔗 Distributed Trace Investigation

• 🤖 Multi-Agent Investigation Workflow

• 📈 AI Confidence & Severity Prediction

• 💡 Actionable Recommendations

• 📑 Executive Incident Reports

• ⚡ End-to-End OpenTelemetry Integration
Key Design Principles

• Observability First — Every AI request is fully traceable.

• Automation Over Manual Debugging — AI performs the investigation.

• Developer-Centric UX — One dashboard instead of multiple tools.

• Explainable AI — Every conclusion is backed by telemetry evidence.

• Production-Ready Architecture — Modular, scalable, and cloud deployable.

System Architecture
“GhostTrace AI follows a complete AI observability pipeline — from user request to AI reasoning, telemetry collection, and investigation analysis — all powered by SigNoz and OpenTelemetry.”
